rows.consequence: External consumers using print-config-schema or print-output-schema can accept objects that JouleWise immediately rejects, and an injected reducer can stage a SummaryMetrics object that the finalized bundle validator later declares invalid. Maintaining three semantic representations increases drift risk in the canonical reproducible flow.
rows.counterevidence: Canonical internal config loading still calls BenchmarkConfig.validate, BundleReader rejects malformed succeeded summaries, and tests/test_schemas.py:257-365 pins emitted-config round trips and hashes. The optional full jsonschema test is skipped when jsonschema is absent, and those tests prove emitted-shape compatibility rather than rejection-equivalence.
evidence_refs: Behavior trace: SummaryMetrics(status=succeeded, energy_request_j=NaN, gross_energy_j=1).to_dict() serialized NaN; _check_summary returned 'energy_request_j is not a finite number'.
Focused tests: tests.test_clock + tests.test_schemas => 25 OK, 1 skipped; external jsonschema probe unavailable because ModuleNotFoundError.
rows.finding: The hand-written exported JSON Schemas and writer-side SummaryMetrics.validate form parallel, weaker validation surfaces than the runtime config and bundle-reader policies. The config schema omits prompt-source exclusivity, suite-ref/hash pairing, and the SSH-host conditional; the summary schema requires only status and permits nullable success metrics, while BundleReader requires the full succeeded key set and finite request/gross energy.

rows.consequence: Type and value provenance can be lost, object strings may be nondeterministic or contain process-specific representations, and downstream validation cannot distinguish captured evidence from a fallback rendering.
rows.counterevidence: The coercion deliberately protects D-011 bundle completion on failure paths; tests/test_controller.py:141-153 injects object() metadata specifically to pin this behavior. That safeguard argues for a structured coercion diagnostic or quarantined value, not simply removing failure-path resilience.
evidence_refs: git grep 'default=str|non.serializable|metadata.*coerc' across pinned joulewise/tests/decision/council/run_reports found the writer, the intentional poison test, and the originating 2026-06-12 run report.
rows.finding: RunBundleWriter.write_metadata silently stringifies every non-JSON-serializable value through json.dumps(default=str), converting malformed adapter evidence into apparently valid metadata without recording which fields were coerced.

rows.consequence: Runtime behavior that produced raw evidence may not be reconstructible from metadata.git_commit, weakening campaign-scale reproducibility and making clean and locally modified harness executions indistinguishable.
rows.counterevidence: Repository operating procedure asks agents to inspect git status, and the later publication-pack specification refuses dirty-tree publication. Those are useful outer gates, but the bounded search found no per-bundle dirty marker or run-time clean-tree gate; a pack hash preserves bundle bytes without recovering which uncommitted source produced them.
evidence_refs: Bounded absence search: grepped git_dirty, dirty-tree, working-tree dirty, git_commit, and git status across pinned joulewise, tests, scripts, and contracts; bundle.py records only HEAD, while dirty handling appears only in outer publication/process tooling.
tests/test_bundle.py:277-279 (bounded cross-boundary test accepts only unknown or a 40-hex commit; no dirty state).
rows.finding: Per-bundle harness provenance records git rev-parse HEAD but does not record whether tracked or untracked source was dirty, so a run made from modified code is labeled with the same commit as a clean run.
